import pandas as pd
import numpy as np


def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    events = inputs["events"].copy()

    # Sort by user_id, then event_ts, then event_id (tie-break)
    events = events.sort_values(
        by=["user_id", "event_ts", "event_id"], kind="mergesort"
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

    # Calendar date (server local) of each event
    events["event_date"] = events["event_ts"].dt.date

    # Identify same-user consecutive rows
    same_user = events["user_id"] == events["user_id"].shift()

    prev_date = events["event_date"].shift()
    prev_ts = events["event_ts"].shift()

    # Different calendar date than previous event (only meaningful when same_user)
    diff_date = events["event_date"] != prev_date

    # Gap in minutes from previous event (only meaningful when same_user)
    gap_minutes = (events["event_ts"] - prev_ts).dt.total_seconds() / 60.0

    # A new session starts when:
    #  - it's the first event for this user (not same_user as previous row), OR
    #  - the calendar date differs from the previous event (same user), OR
    #  - the gap from the previous event (same user, same date) is > 45 minutes
    new_session = (~same_user) | (same_user & diff_date) | (same_user & (gap_minutes > 45))

    events["new_session_flag"] = new_session

    # Cumulative sum per user gives the session number (1-based)
    events["session_num"] = (
        events.groupby("user_id")["new_session_flag"].cumsum().astype("int64")
    )

    # Aggregate into sessions
    user_sessions = events.groupby(
        ["user_id", "session_num"], as_index=False
    ).agg(
        session_date=("event_date", "first"),
        session_start=("event_ts", "min"),
        session_end=("event_ts", "max"),
        event_count=("event_id", "count"),
    )

    # Ensure correct dtypes
    user_sessions["user_id"] = user_sessions["user_id"].astype("int64")
    user_sessions["session_num"] = user_sessions["session_num"].astype("int64")
    user_sessions["session_start"] = user_sessions["session_start"].astype("datetime64[us]")
    user_sessions["session_end"] = user_sessions["session_end"].astype("datetime64[us]")
    user_sessions["event_count"] = user_sessions["event_count"].astype("int64")
    # session_date should remain a plain date object (no time component)

    # Sort output by user_id, session_num
    user_sessions = user_sessions.sort_values(
        by=["user_id", "session_num"]
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

    user_sessions = user_sessions[
        ["user_id", "session_num", "session_date", "session_start", "session_end", "event_count"]
    ]

    return {"user_sessions": user_sessions}
